faqs.question: Do we make rangoli on Ganesh Chaturthi?
faqs.answer: Yes, and usually twice over: one at the doorway and one on the floor in front of the mandap. It is drawn on the morning of the sthapana, which in 2026 is Monday 14 September, before the first aarti.

faqs.question: How long does a Ganesh Chaturthi rangoli actually take?
faqs.answer: A 5x5-dot kolam takes 10–15 minutes. A coloured Ganesha face runs 60–90 minutes, and a three-foot marigold pookalam takes 45–60 minutes with two people. Kolam practitioners interviewed in Pondicherry put a daily design at fifteen or twenty minutes and a festival one at an hour or two.

faqs.question: Which design is easiest if I have never drawn one?
faqs.answer: The 5x5 pulli kolam. Twenty-five dots spaced about 5 cm apart, then one closed curve around them, and the dots tell you immediately when a line has gone wrong.

faqs.question: How much rangoli powder do I need for a 3-foot design?
faqs.answer: Roughly 400–600 g if you are filling about six square feet across four to six shades. That is an estimate from line length rather than a weighed figure, so buy a kilo if you also want a daily threshold design.

faqs.question: Is rice flour better than the coloured powder from the market?
faqs.answer: For the doorway, yes. Rice flour is the traditional material and it feeds ants and birds, which is the point of the drawing. The market colour packets are unregulated: sampling of dry Holi powders in Kolkata found lead at nearly twice the FDA cosmetic limit and endotoxin around 35 times the dermatological reference.

faqs.question: Will the rangoli survive people walking over it for ten days?
faqs.answer: No. A floor design typically disappears under passers-by's feet within a few hours. Plan on redrawing a small one daily rather than protecting a large one.

faqs.question: Do I have to redraw it every day of the festival?
faqs.answer: Only if you want one every day. The workable pattern is one large design on the sthapana morning plus a 15-minute threshold kolam each day, which totals about 2.5 hours across the ten days to 25 September.

faqs.question: Should the rangoli go at the door or in front of the mandap?
faqs.answer: Both if there is time, the mandap one if there is not. The doorway design greets arrivals but takes all the footfall; the mandap design is protected and is the one that appears in photographs.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a rangoli and a kolam?
faqs.answer: Kolam is the South Indian threshold practice, usually white rice flour drawn around a dot lattice, split into kambi (straight lines) and sikku (curves). Rangoli is the broader term and is more often filled with colour.

faqs.question: Can I use flowers instead of powder?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is currently the cheapest big design. Loose marigolds and chrysanthemums were at ₹10–20 per kilo wholesale in Pune on 4 September 2026, and about a kilo covers a three-foot circle.

faqs.question: What do I do with the rangoli at visarjan?
faqs.answer: Sweep the flour away with the floor, compost the petals, and bin synthetic coloured powder rather than washing it into a drain. Do not carry the powder to the water with the murti.

faqs.question: Does SubhSandesh have a rangoli tool?
faqs.answer: No. The platform makes shareable personalised pages, not floor designs, and it will not help you draw. It matters for the other half of the greeting: 49.6% of the 46,005 recorded page views were opened on a phone.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Ganesh Chaturthi Rangoli Designs: 25 Dots to Nine Square Feet

Ganesh Chaturthi rangoli designs get drawn on the morning of the sthapana — Monday 14 September 2026 — in two places: the threshold, and the floor in front of the mandap. Choose by the time you actually have.

A 5x5-dot pulli kolam is 10–15 minutes and about one square foot. A coloured Ganesha face or a marigold pookalam is 60–120 minutes and six to nine square feet, and it will be walked over by evening.

Time is the constraint nobody mentions, and the only festival SubhSandesh has measured says so bluntly. Across the 3,894 personalised pages built on the platform since 12 March 2026, a Raksha Bandhan sample of 89 pages showed a median lead time of 0 days: 49.4% were made on the festival day itself, and 24 of those 44 same-day pages were finished before noon. Pick the design you can finish before the aarti.

## Where it goes: two designs, threshold then mandap, before the first aarti

In its home tradition the kolam is a threshold drawing, made each day before dawn during the Brahma muhurtam on the floors of houses, temples and shops across Tamil Nadu and Pondicherry. Two lines on an ordinary day; more on a special one.

A Ganesh Chaturthi rangoli inherits that logic and adds a second site. The doorway design greets arrivals; the mandap design frames the murti and ends up in the photographs. If there is time for only one, draw the mandap one.

## Five designs, timed: 25 dots to nine square feet

The basis, stated. Times are anchored to the only field measurement I could find — interviews in Pondicherry with two women of thirty years' practice, who put a daily kolam at "fifteen or twenty minutes" and a festival kolam at "an hour or two of labour".

Floor area is arithmetic from a dot grid spaced about 5 cm apart. Powder weights are estimates from line length, not weighed quantities.

| Design | Dots (pulli) | Floor area | Time to draw | Material at that size |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5x5 pulli kolam (star or lotus) | 25 | ~1 sq ft, 30 cm square | 10–15 min | ~50 g rice flour, kitchen stock |
| 7x7 sikku kolam (curved loops) | 49 | ~2 sq ft | 20–30 min | ~100 g rice flour, kitchen stock |
| Om, swastik and modak border | freehand on a 5-dot centre line | ~3 sq ft | 30–40 min | ~150 g flour plus 2 colour shades |
| Ganesha face, filled with colour | freehand, no grid | ~6 sq ft | 60–90 min | 400–600 g powder across 4–6 shades |
| Marigold pookalam (petals only) | none | ~9 sq ft, 3 ft circle | 45–60 min, two pairs of hands | ~1 kg loose marigold |

One 1 kg pack of rice flour covers every powder row here once, the Ganesha face taking two-thirds of it.

### 5x5 pulli kolam — the one that fits a 15-minute window

Twenty-five dots, one closed curve, no colour. Draw this one if the murti arrives at 9 a.m. and you are also cooking; it is the only row here a beginner gets right first time.

### 7x7 sikku kolam — one unbroken line around 49 dots

Sikku means the curved, knot-like family, as against kambi, which is predominantly straight lines. Forty-nine dots doubles the floor area and roughly doubles the time, and the payoff is that a single continuous line reads as skill from across a room.

### Om, swastik and modak border — the motifs people actually want

Three small motifs rather than one design, which is why it survives a busy doorway: you redraw the damaged motif, not the whole thing. Budget 30–40 minutes and two colour shades.

### Ganesha face in colour — six square feet and up to 90 minutes

The design every image board shows, and the one whose cost is never stated. Freehand outline, then four to six shades filled in, at 60–90 minutes and 400–600 g of powder. Do this once, on the sthapana morning, in front of the mandap.

### Marigold pookalam — no dots, no chalk, and cheap this week

Petals in concentric rings, no grid, so two people do a three-foot circle in under an hour. Loose marigolds and chrysanthemums were ₹10–20 per kilo wholesale in Pune on 4 September 2026 — a supply glut, not a normal rate — which makes this the cheapest large design going.

## Material: rice flour, kola-podi, or a packet carrying twice the FDA lead limit

The traditional material is rice flour, or finely ground rice powder called kola-podi in Tamil, and the choice is not decorative: flour on the floor feeds ants, birds and insects, which is why the drawing is described as hospitality rather than ornament. Chalk and stone powder are the cost-cutting substitutes, and they feed nothing.

Coloured packets are worth pausing on. The nearest published measurement is on dry Holi powders, not rangoli shades: samples collected across Kolkata carried lead at almost twice the FDA's maximum permissible limit for cosmetics, and endotoxin at roughly 35 times the dermatological safety reference.

That study measured Holi colours, and I found no equivalent analysis of rangoli powder — but both come off the same unregulated shelf, often labelled herbal with no ingredient list. Keep toddlers off a coloured design and wash hands before the modak.

## Durability: gone in a few hours, so budget for ten redraws to 25 September

A kolam is designed to be temporary. It disappears under the feet of passers-by within a few hours, which is the honest answer to whether a design will "last" the festival: it will not.

Ganesh Chaturthi 2026 runs from 14 September to Anant Chaturdashi on Friday 25 September. Ten daily 5x5 kolams cost about 2.5 hours in total across the festival. Ten Ganesha faces cost 15 hours, which nobody does.

The workable pattern is one large design on the sthapana morning and a 15-minute threshold kolam each day after, redrawn rather than repaired. Keep the elaborate work beside the mandap, where footfall is controlled.

## What the 49.4% figure is, and what it is not

Two disclosures, because the number is load-bearing here.

First, that measurement is **Raksha Bandhan, not Ganesh Chaturthi** — a different festival, and a one-day one. Ganesh Chaturthi runs ten days, so a same-day rush is suggestive of festival behaviour, not measured for this festival. Second, **n = 89 is small**: it will not support a per-region or per-template rate, and no count of Ganesh pages can be projected from it.

What it does support is the shape. Of the 79 pages finished in time, 55.7% were made on the day and 86.1% within 24 hours of it, and the median gap from first save to last edit was 5.4 hours in that festival sample — against 6.8 hours sampled on the platform's romantic pages. One sitting, on the day.

The limiter belongs here too: occasion-dated pages are 144 of 3,894, 3.7% of everything built here. A real measurement of a small slice.

## The geometry: pulli, kambi, sikku, and a 125,501-dot proof

The dotted family has a formal structure. A pulli kolam is built on a symmetrical lattice of dots — pulli is Tamil for dot — around which lines and arcs are drawn until an enclosed pattern contains every dot, and those patterns split into kambi (mostly straight lines) and sikku (mostly curves).

Published in npj Heritage Science on 9 March 2026, Sivakumar and Sivakumar's open-access algorithm generates one-stroke kolams around such a grid, the largest a 501-dimension pattern of 125,501 anchor-dots drawn as one continuous trace. The authors flag the obvious risk: automating an artform can separate it from the people who hold it.

The practical use of this is error-correction: lay and count the dots first, and a wrong curve shows immediately, before 40 minutes of powder is committed to it.

## Where a rangoli loses: 49.6% of 46,005 page views were on a phone

A rangoli is the one Ganesh Chaturthi decoration you cannot buy, delegate or send. It exists on your floor for a few hours, and a cousin in Dubai will only ever see a photograph of it. No design choice fixes that.

SubhSandesh does not help you draw one. It does the half that travels: of 46,005 recorded views of shared pages, 49.6% were opened on a phone, which is where the photo ends up anyway.

The closest equivalent is a [Ganesh Chaturthi page the recipient performs themselves](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-ganesh-chaturthi) — they offer the durva and modak, and the aarti thali circles — with a [step-by-step build guide](https://subhsandesh.in/guides/happy-ganesh-chaturthi) for it. The [hand-tied digital bouquet](https://subhsandesh.in/bouquet-gf) works the way a pookalam does, by arranging blooms into a pattern.

## At visarjan on 25 September: sweep the flour, compost the petals

Rice flour needs no disposal plan — the ants will have handled most of it. Sweep the rest with the floor.

Petals should be composted rather than carried to the water with the murti. Bin synthetic coloured powder rather than washing it into a drain, given what the Kolkata sampling found in comparable festival powders.

## Watch the page get built

Ninety seconds, start to finish — the aarti going round, the five offerings, and the box at the end where they write a line back to you: [Ganesh Chaturthi Wishes Online — Full Walkthrough](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mpWiv5T59QY). More page walkthroughs on Instagram: [@subhsandesh_official](https://www.instagram.com/subhsandesh_official).

## Sources

- Sivakumar and Sivakumar, ["An algorithm for one-stroke kolam generation using a gating structure"](https://www.nature.com/articles/s40494-026-02310-3), *npj Heritage Science* 14:144, 9 March 2026, CC BY 4.0 — pulli/kambi/sikku, rice flour as hospitality, a 125,501-dot one-stroke kolam.
- Ketaki Chowkhani, ["Kolam and the Making of Tamil Femininity"](https://www.sahapedia.org/kolam-and-the-making-of-tamil-femininity), Sahapedia, no date given — daily kolams "fifteen or twenty minutes", festival kolams "an hour or two of labour".
- Sahapedia, ["Significance of Kolam in Tamil Culture"](https://www.sahapedia.org/significance-of-kolam-tamil-culture), no date given — rice flour or kola-podi, chalk and stone powder as cost-cutting substitutes, the design lost under passers-by's feet within hours.
- ["A Study of the Levels of Some Toxic Substances present in Dry Holi Colours in Kolkata, India"](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8994014/), *Indian Journal of Clinical Biochemistry* 37(2):206–211, 18 April 2021 — lead at almost twice, endotoxin at roughly 35 times, FDA reference limits.
- FloralDaily, ["Flower prices crash in Pune ahead of Ganapati festival"](https://www.floraldaily.com/article/9869516/india-flower-prices-crash-in-pune-ahead-of-ganapati-festival/), 4 September 2026 — marigolds at ₹10–20 per kg wholesale on a supply glut.

auditReport.honestAssessment: An answer engine would cite this over the ranking assets for one reason: it is the only page on this query that states what a Ganesh Chaturthi rangoli costs in minutes, floor area and material — 25 dots and 10-15 minutes against six square feet and 60-90 minutes — with the basis of every figure named, plus the one thing an image board cannot carry, that a floor design is gone under footfall in hours and therefore means ten redraws to 25 September. The blunt limitation is format, not writing: page one for this keyword on the India-localised SERP is three Pinterest boards, an Instagram reel, two YouTube tutorials and a Shutterstock search page, with no AI Overview and no featured snippet, because the intent is 'show me a picture I can copy' and Google is serving it correctly. A prose page should not be expected to take position 1 here; the realistic targets are the PAA slot 'Do we make rangoli on Ganesh Chaturthi?', constrained long-tail queries about time, powder quantity and durability, and answer-engine citation, where extractable prose with numbers beats a board with none. Against that, the domain is far below the entrenched platforms and the first-party anchor is a small n=89 sample from a different festival, so this is a bet on the constraint questions, not on the head term.
